title: News headline sentiment per ticker and day with FinBERT and a VADER baseline
description:
Scores the tone of financial news headlines and aggregates it into one row per ticker and trading day. The output is a sentiment time series you can chart next to prices or use as one input in your own research.

  • FinBERT (ProsusAI/finbert on Hugging Face, via the transformers pipeline): a BERT model fine-tuned on financial news sentences. It returns probabilities for positive, negative and neutral; the score is P(positive) minus P(negative), from -1 to 1. Runs locally on CPU.
  • VADER as a baseline: a rule-based lexicon with no model download, useful to compare against and as a fallback. It was built for social media and misreads finance terms.
  • Ticker extraction from a tickers column and cashtags ($AAPL, $BRK.B).
  • Daily aggregation in the exchange time zone (default New York). Headlines after the 16:00 close count for the next day. Syndicated copies of the same headline are counted once.

Not investment advice. The output describes the tone of headlines. It is not a price forecast or a trading signal, and this example makes no claim that it predicts market movements.
implementationSteps: Collect headlines with publication time and, where available, tickers from a news API or RSS feed you are licensed to use, and save them as CSV (published_at, headline, tickers).
Extract tickers from the tickers column and from cashtags in the headline; drop headlines without a ticker.
Score all headlines in batches with the transformers text-classification pipeline (ProsusAI/finbert, top_k=None) and compute score = P(positive) - P(negative).
Optionally score the same headlines with VADER to compare and to spot where the general-purpose lexicon disagrees with FinBERT.
Convert publication times to the exchange time zone and assign news after the 16:00 close to the next day.
Remove syndicated duplicates per ticker and day, then aggregate: headline count, mean score, share of positive and negative headlines.
Write the daily table to CSV and review a sample of scored headlines by hand before using the series in any analysis.
performance:
Targets and expectations, not measured results.

  • Target: label agreement with a hand-labeled sample of 200 of your own headlines of at least 80 % for FinBERT, and clearly above the VADER baseline. Measure it; financial wording differs between sources.
  • FinBERT is a BERT-base model (about 110 million parameters). It runs on a CPU; throughput depends on the machine and batch size, so measure it before planning a large backfill (a GPU helps there).
  • Days with one or two headlines give noisy averages; the headline count is in the output so you can filter them.
  • No claim is made about predicting prices. Any such use needs its own out-of-sample evaluation with costs, and this example does not provide one.
userExperience: An analyst runs python -m sentiment.cli headlines.csv daily.csv and gets a CSV with ticker, day, headlines, mean_score, positive_share, negative_share, for example ACME, 2026-03-02, 3, 0.1, 0.333, 0.333. Every run prints the reminder that the output is headline tone only and not investment advice. Switching to the VADER baseline is one flag (--scorer vader).
